items.title: The dualizing module represents the functor given by top cohomology of the fibre dimension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For X over a local base A with dualizing module omega_X as in Example labelled example-proper-over-local, with d = dim(X_s) the dimension of the closed fibre, the lemma asserts that if dim(X) = d + dim(A) then omega_X represents the functor F -> Hom_A(H^d(X, F), omega_A) on coherent O_X-modules (statement lines 6156-6196). The proof runs a six term chain of equalities: Hom_X(F, omega_X) = Ext^{-dim(X)}_X(F, omega_X^bullet), using that H^i(omega_X^bullet) vanishes for i < -dim(X) by Lemma labelled lemma-vanishing-good-dualizing and Derived Categories, Lemma labelled derived-lemma-negative-exts; the shift reinterpretation of Ext by definition; the identification of omega_X^bullet with f^!(omega_A^bullet); the adjunction f^! of Rf_* from Lemma labelled lemma-twisted-inverse-image; and finally the reduction to Hom_A(H^d(X, F), omega_A), which uses that R^if_*F vanishes for i > d by Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma labelled coherent-lemma-higher-direct-images-zero-above-dimension-fibre and that H^j(omega_A^bullet) vanishes for j < -dim(A) (proof lines 6198-6212). Reading the representing object off the dualizing complex through the vanishing ranges of the pushforwards is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
